Where our story begins

The Lisu People

A mountain people of southwest China, Myanmar and northern Thailand, who carried their stories, and their silver, across borders for generations.

A people of the mountains

From the high valleys of Yunnan

The Lisu speak a Tibeto-Burman language, related to Lahu, Akha and Yi. For centuries they lived in the high river valleys of southwest China. Over generations, families moved south along the mountains, from the upper Yangtze to the Salween valley, then into Burma.

The first Lisu families reached northern Thailand between 1900 and 1930. Today tens of thousands of Lisu live in Thailand, nearly half of them in Chiang Mai province.

Silver

Wealth you could carry

For a people who often had to move, wealth had to travel with them. Silver jewelry was the family’s principal wealth, worn by women and men on the wrists, neck, ears and chest. Lisu silversmiths made it to order, for Lisu families.

Many pieces carry the natural world. In one Chiang Mai village’s silver tradition, the fish stands for abundance, the butterfly for beauty, and the chrysanthemum for vitality. Meanings differ from family to family.

“There are no rich, no poor.”

A saying of the Lisu New Year
New Year

The year’s most beautiful day

Lisu New Year falls with Chinese New Year. Families dress in their finest clothes, women wear their full silver, and the village dances around a tree planted for the celebration.

The soul

Calling the spirit home

In traditional Lisu belief, a person carries more than one soul: seven for a woman, nine for a man. A soul can wander when someone is frightened or unsettled, and it can be called home. A thread is then tied around the wrist. Our first collection is inspired by that thread.

Today

A culture being kept

Lisu life has changed. Many Lisu now live in cities, and Lisu families today may be Christian, Buddhist or follow the old ways. Yet many young Lisu are choosing to wear Lisu dress again, and to tell their own stories.

Lisu Soul is part of that: a Lisu mother and daughter in Chiang Mai, sharing their heritage in silver, one story at a time.

A Father Calls His Child’s Spirit Home

A Lisu-Inspired Silver Bracelet Collection

Limited Edition · 925 Sterling Silver

Rooted in Lisu heritage, this collection draws inspiration from Cho-Ha-Khua (โช-ฮา-ควัว), the traditional Lisu practice of calling the spirit home.

In this tradition, a thread is prepared through ritual and prayer before being tied around the wrist. It carries the meaning of blessings, protection, good health, compassion, prosperity, and safe journeys, reflecting the hopes and wishes passed on to those we hold dear.

Inspired by this meaningful thread, we reimagine its symbolism in 925 sterling silver, transforming a traditional symbol into a contemporary bracelet that connects cultural heritage with modern life.

Designed to accompany you wherever life takes you, each piece serves as a reminder of your roots, the people who care for you, and the blessings you carry along the way.

No matter how far you travel, may your spirit stay with you — and may your heart always know the way home.

A limited-edition collection inspired by Lisu heritage, belonging, and the enduring bond between generations.

Our Story, Now Yours.

Our story begins with the Lisu people, but it doesn’t end within our community. Through jewelry, our stories travel beyond borders, becoming part of the lives of people from different backgrounds and cultures.

It’s about connection — sharing our heritage in a way that brings people closer to our culture, not as outsiders looking in, but as people who can connect with and become part of the story.
